title: P03a — Expose immutable effect placement timing
description:
## Shared prerequisite for catalog adaptations
Own stdlib plus focused player/toolchain/specification bridges after P17 releases those checkouts. Preserve D02 absolute integer seek; never introduce a wall clock.
Add optional readonly timing:{startFrame,endFrame} to EffectMountContext for source compatibility. mountEffect always supplies a fresh frozen interval copied from validated EffectConfig; caller mutation after mount cannot alter visibility or local timing. New catalog implementations that animate relative to placement calculate local seconds=(absoluteFrame-startFrame)/fps and explicitly clamp their authored timeline endpoints. Do not retime existing version1 effects (echo/particles) or silently change accepted P08a fixtures. Direct mounting of a new effect requiring timing fails EFFECT_TIMING_UNAVAILABLE if absent; documented mountEffect is the normal public path.
Tests: nonzero start,24/30fps, frames before/inside/after interval, reverse/repeated/random/partition seeks, caller config mutation, unchanged existing effect pixels. Prove copied XML/player/normal packed CLI matches with an offset test effect and a zero-offset fixture. Document timing contract and pure timeline adapters. Primary accepts; no worker closure/commits. Follow one-writer-per-checkout and one heavy slot.
Primary review clarification: preserve existing XML/player/renderer rounding exactly: startFrame=floor(authoredStartSeconds*fps), endFrame=ceil(authoredEndSeconds*fps). Copy validated config bounds for visibility AND readonly timing context before mount; later caller mutation must affect neither. Test fractional-second boundaries at24/30fps.
Primary compatibility correction: actual integration revealed ComposableRenderer culls frame effects using exact seconds before mount, omitting the leading frame at fractional starts even though the player and effect controller include floor(startSec*fps). Fix culling for FrameEffect only to the same half-open [floor(start*fps),ceil(end*fps)) interval. Preserve ordinary component culling, absolute effect seeks, interpolation and integer-boundary/reference fixture pixels. The old requirement to preserve all v1 boundary pixels is narrowed explicitly: formerly omitted fractional boundary frames are intentionally corrected to establish copied XML/player/packed CLI parity. Prove leading/trailing fractional frames at24/30fps and document this specific compatibility fix; do not weaken parity tests to preserve the discrepancy.
